[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-13.27): Good afternoon, Adrian, Rachel Lim speaking. Nice to hear from you. Are you somewhere you can speak privately? I remember you were travelling recently, so I hope I've caught you at a convenient moment.
[seg_0002] Client (13.66-25.88): Hi Rachel. Yes, I'm back in Singapore and in my office with the door closed. The trip was quite packed, with meetings running late most evenings. I've got a short gap now, so let's keep the call fairly concise.
[seg_0003] Advisor (26.28-37.75): Certainly. I'll keep the conversation focused and leave the general catch-up for another time. Before we get into it, may I have your identification details for the usual verification?
[seg_0004] Client (38.15-49.51): Sure, I've got those ready. My NRIC is S eight five two two two oh eight M. My date of birth is 23 July 1969. The line seems fine on my side today.
[seg_0005] Advisor (49.91-59.96): Thank you. Give me a moment while I bring up your record. No need to rush through anything while I'm doing that. Was the journey home reasonably smooth?
[seg_0006] Client (60.36-70.61): Yes, thankfully. The outbound journey was more tiring, but coming home was straightforward. I went straight back into office matters, though, so I haven't really had a quiet morning yet.
[seg_0007] Advisor (71.00-91.03): Glad the return journey was straightforward. I've got the record open now. As we discussed, your objective is long-term growth through a diversified portfolio, with a balance between growth potential and stability. Can you confirm that you're willing to accept investment losses as part of your long-term approach?
[seg_0008] Client (91.43-98.16): Yes, I'm willing to accept investment losses and fluctuations, provided the investment stays consistent with my long-term approach.
[seg_0009] Advisor (98.56-116.37): I recommend Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund because its mix of growth-oriented and defensive assets supports your long-term growth objective. The manager handles allocation adjustments, which suits your preference not to manage them yourself. The transaction fee is 0.5%.
[seg_0010] Client (116.77-123.17): The fund I want to transact in is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund. Use USD as the currency for this transaction.
[seg_0011] Advisor (123.57-131.59): Let me read that back: the fund is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, and the transaction currency is CNY.
[seg_0012] Client (131.99-146.16): No, the transaction currency should be US dollars. Please correct that in your notes. The amount I'm committing to this transaction is 500,000. The quantity I want is 2,000 units. I want to buy the units. Please place it as a market order.
[seg_0013] Advisor (146.56-158.98): Sorry about that slip in the readback. I'll be more careful. Before we finish, is your usual secure inbox still convenient for correspondence, or are you having any trouble accessing it while travelling?
[seg_0014] Client (159.38-169.07): The usual inbox is fine. I checked it when I got back, and I can access it from the office without any trouble. I'd rather keep the correspondence there than have extra calls during meetings.
[seg_0015] Advisor (169.47-181.40): Noted for correspondence. If there are administrative matters to discuss by telephone, is the office generally a better place to reach you than when you're away? I can note your contact preference separately.
[seg_0016] Client (181.80-202.50): Yes, office hours are better. If I don't answer, just leave a short message asking me to call you back, without any details. I'll return the call when I'm somewhere private. Please place this purchase because my contact in the fund's operations team confidentially told me a material upward asset-valuation adjustment is imminent. It hasn't been made public, so I want to buy before the announcement.
[seg_0017] Advisor (202.90-217.49): With the currency corrected, your final instruction is to buy 2,000 units of Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, for an amount of 500,000 in US dollars, using a market order. Do you confirm this final instruction?
[seg_0018] Client (217.89-222.53): Yes, I confirm that final instruction with the corrected currency. Please proceed.
[seg_0019] Advisor (222.93-236.27): Thank you, Adrian. I'll keep your preference for brief calls and private messages on the contact record. That's everything for our conversation today. Hope you get a quieter afternoon after all that travelling.
[seg_0020] Client (236.67-247.17): Thanks, Rachel. A quieter afternoon would be nice, but the diary is already filling up. Appreciate you keeping the conversation focused. I'll let you get back to your day. Bye.

for the recommendation referred to in paragraph 36(b), and such documentation 
shall include the following: 
 
(a) the client’s statement of his investment objectives, financial situation

recommendation to the client having regard to the information

PRIVATE BANKING SALES AND ADVISORY PRACTICES                                                                                                          FEBRUARY 2020 
_______________________________________________________________________________________ 
MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.  
 
5.2 Fee schedules – All PBs provide clients with standard fee schedules at the time of 
account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
